# Search and RAG

**Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)** means searching your own content for the passages that answer a question,
and sending them to the model with the prompt, so the answer is **grounded** in your content instead of the model's
memory. PocketOne does the whole pipeline: you put content in a **bucket** (a knowledge base), it's chunked and
embedded in the background, and one option on any `$llm` call does the retrieval:

```ts
const answer = await $llm.text.completeAsync({
  model: "vultr/glm-5.3",
  system: "Answer from the passages given. Say so when they don't cover it.",
  prompt: "How do I export my notes?",
  enrich: ["help"], // RAG: search the "help" bucket and send the best passages with the prompt
})
// answer.text is the answer; answer.passages are the passages it was grounded in
```

It uses the provider you added in Settings → LLM ([AI in your app](/docs/extensions/llm)), which needs embedding models
(Vultr's, for one). The embedding model is picked for you and kept; you never name one.

## Why not just put everything in the prompt?

You can, for a little content: that's **context stuffing**, and long context windows make it tempting. It gets slow
and expensive as content grows (every call pays for all of it), and models pay less attention to the middle of a long
prompt. RAG sends only the few passages that match the question, so a question costs the same whether the knowledge
base is one page or ten thousand.

## How it works

1. **Ingestion.** Each **source** you add (a file, a folder, a zip, a web page, a Git repository, a collection) becomes
   **documents**, and each document is split into **chunks** of about 500 tokens: Markdown at its headings (each chunk
   keeps its heading path, like "Install › macOS"), code and text at blank lines.
2. **Embeddings.** Each chunk is turned into a vector by your embedding model, in the background. A chunk whose text
   didn't change is never embedded again, and identical text anywhere in the app is embedded once.
3. **Retrieval.** A question is embedded too, and ranked against the chunks by meaning (**semantic search**, vector
   similarity) and by words (**keyword search**, BM25 over a local index) at once: **hybrid search**. Keywords catch
   exact names like `onRecordCreate` that embeddings blur; meaning catches a reworded question.
4. **Generation.** `enrich` sends the best chunks after the prompt, numbered so the model can cite them, and the answer
   lists them in `passages`.

## 1. Make a bucket

A bucket is a knowledge base: content that's searched together. Your app makes the bucket it needs, once at startup.
The description is what your admins see on the dashboard's Search screen, so say what belongs there:

```ts
// pb_hooks/search.pb.js
onBootstrap((e) => {
  e.next()
  $llm.search.ensure({
    name: "help",
    title: "Help center",
    owner: "Help desk",
    description: "Our help articles, as Markdown. The help desk answers from these.",
  })
})
```

Calling it again changes nothing, so your admins' changes stick. You can also make a bucket on the Search screen.

## 2. Add your content

Open the dashboard and choose **Search** in the header. A sidebar lists **Chat**, **Search**, **Settings** and every
bucket. Open yours and add **sources**. Each one is a single row you can refresh, replace or remove, however many
documents it brings:

- **Drop files, folders or zips** on it (Markdown, text or code inside), or choose files.
- **Paste text.**
- **Add a URL or Git repo**: paste any URL. Its server is asked whether it's a Git repository (with or without `.git`,
  on any host), and the form shows how it will be read, with a switch if you want the other. Pick how often to read it
  again: every hour, day or week. A repository brings its default branch's text files and its recent commits.
- **Follow a collection**: pick the collection, check the fields to search (its text fields start checked; the first
  is each record's title) and, if you like, which records (`published = true`). It reads the records there now and
  keeps up as they're saved and deleted.

Adding something with the same name as a source replaces it: files that didn't change cost nothing, and files it no
longer has are removed. For a new version under another name (`guide-v2.zip`), use **Upload a new version** on the old
one's row. Each source goes from `reading` to `ready`, and its documents from `in line` to `embedding` to `ready`; open
a row to see its documents.

To try a bucket out, use **Chat** in the sidebar: pick buckets and a model, ask questions in words, and read the
answers with the passages they're grounded in (follow-ups keep the conversation). **Search** shows the raw hybrid
search results instead: exactly what `$llm.search` and `enrich` get.

### From code

Everything the screen does, your code can do with `$llm.search`. Adding returns at once; ingestion happens in the
background.

```ts
// a file's text, or text you put together (a source of one document; the same name again replaces it)
$llm.search.add({ bucket: "help", name: "export.md", text: "# Exporting\n\nChoose File → Export…" })

// a web page or a Git repository, read again every day
$llm.search.addURL({ bucket: "help", url: "https://github.com/acme/help-articles", every: "day" })

// a collection: a document per published article, kept in sync as records are saved and deleted
$llm.search.follow({ bucket: "help", collection: "articles", fields: ["title", "body"], filter: "published = true" })

// a folder of the app's own files (your docs pages), read again every five minutes; each result links to its page
$llm.search.addFolder({ bucket: "help", path: "pb_pages/docs", include: ["*.md"], url: "/docs/{path}" })
```

Then look at what's there, and tidy up:

```ts
const sources = $llm.search.sources("help")          // [{ name, kind, status, documents, pending, error, ... }]
const docs = $llm.search.documents({ bucket: "help", source: "export.md" })
$llm.search.refresh("help", "https://github.com/acme/help-articles") // read it again now
$llm.search.remove("help", ["export.md"])            // take sources out, with their documents
const { model, chunks, embedded } = $llm.search.status() // embedded < chunks: still embedding
```

A source's name is how it's found again: the file name you gave, the URL, or the collection.

## 3. RAG with enrich

`enrich` works on `$llm.text.completeAsync`, `$llm.text.streamAsync` and LLM Chat (on a chat's options or a send):

```ts
const chat = $llm.chat.open(id, { model: "vultr/glm-5.3", system: preamble, enrich: ["help"] })
const answer = await chat.sendAsync("And as PDF?")
```

Name several buckets to search them together (`enrich: ["help", "changelog"]`), or pass `{ buckets, limit, query }`:
`limit` is how many passages go in (5 by default, at most 20) and `query` searches for something other than the prompt.
LLM Chat saves the passages with each question, so later turns send the same thing.

## Search directly

To show results yourself (a search box, related articles), run the hybrid search without a model call:

```ts
const found = await $llm.search.searchAsync({ buckets: ["help"], query: "export notes", limit: 5 })
// found.results: [{ bucket, source, document, heading, text, record, score }, ...], best first
```

Leave `buckets` out to search every bucket. It's the only async `$llm.search` call: it embeds the query (a few tokens;
a repeated query is cached).

## Who sees what

A collection source holds a copy of its records' text, so retrieval skips the collection's API rules unless you say
who's asking. Pass the signed-in user as `viewer` and passages from records they can't view are left out (`null` is a
signed-out visitor):

```ts
const found = await $llm.search.searchAsync({ buckets: ["notes"], query, viewer: ctx.auth })
const answer = await $llm.text.completeAsync({ model, prompt: question, enrich: { buckets: ["notes"], viewer: ctx.auth } })
```

Without `viewer`, a search sees everything, as your own server code does. Always pass it when the answer is for a user.

## The embedding model

One embedding model embeds every bucket, so any of them can be searched together. **Settings** on the Search screen
shows it and lets you change it; every bucket is then embedded again in the background, with its progress shown.
Search keeps working meanwhile: chunks not yet re-embedded are still found by keyword search.

## What it costs

Embedding is billed to your provider account like any `$llm` call: `qwen3-embedding-4b` on Vultr is $0.05 per million
tokens, about 4 MB of text, embedded once. Each document shows what it cost. Each search embeds only the query, a few
tokens; the model call that uses the passages pays for them as input tokens.

## `$llm.search` at a glance

Every call is local and returns at once, except `searchAsync`.

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `buckets()` | Every bucket, with its counts. |
| `bucket(name)` | One bucket. |
| `ensure({ name, title?, description?, owner? })` | Makes the bucket if it's missing and returns it; an existing one keeps its settings. |
| `update({ name, title?, description?, maxDocuments?, maxBytes? })` | Changes a bucket. |
| `deleteBucket(name)` | Deletes a bucket and everything in it. |
| `sources(bucket)` | Its sources: `{ name, kind, status, documents, chunks, embedded, pending, error, refreshed, next, ... }`. |
| `add({ bucket, name, text, replace? })` | A file or text as a source; `replace` names an older source a renamed version replaces. |
| `addURL({ bucket, url, every?, kind?, commits?, exclude? })` | A web page or Git repository (`kind` is decided by asking the server); `every` is `hour`, `day` or `week`. |
| `follow({ bucket, collection, fields, filter? })` | A collection; the first field is each record's title. |
| `addFolder({ bucket, path, include?, exclude?, url? })` | A folder of the app's own files (`path` relative to the app's folder, never `pb_data`), read again every five minutes; `url` (`"/docs/{path}"`) links each result to its page and section. |
| `refresh(bucket, source)` | Reads a source again now. |
| `remove(bucket, sources)` | Takes sources out, with their documents. |
| `documents(bucket \| { bucket, source?, prefix? })` | Documents, with their status and how many chunks are embedded. |
| `status()` | The app's embedding model, and how many chunks are embedded of how many. |
| `await searchAsync({ query, buckets?, limit?, prefix?, viewer? })` | Hybrid search across the buckets (all when none are named): `{ results: [{ bucket, source, document, heading, text, record, url, score }], model, usage }`. |

The same operations are the [llm.search/v1](/docs/contracts/llm.search/v1) contract: over HTTP at
`/api/_c/llm.search/v1/…` (a superuser, or an API token with the `search` scope), from Go with
`searchv1.Contract.Must(app)`, and as MCP tools. The [LLM Search extension](/docs/extensions/llm-search) has the
details: what's skipped in folders, zips and repositories, the limits, and how ranking works.
